searchText: Does `MAX_CELLS_IN_EXTENDED_MATRIX` need to be a config value? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/_features/eip7594/das-core.md#data-size It's based on `MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK` and would need to be increased as well when we increase blob count. May not be an issue (we're not using it atm), but thought worth checking here No not really. That's an artifact of `ExtendedMatrix` which no longer exists. Right now, the config value is used to define the return type for two functions. We could change them to return a `Sequence[MatrixEntry]` instead. Does Lighthouse use an "extended matrix" similar to the spec? We don't use the intermediate type at the moment, and just transform returned the cells and proofs into `DataColumnSidecars` directly Makes sense. I think most clients do something like that. That configuration value is specific to the spec's implementation, which isn't necessarily the best way to do things.

excerpts.author: jimmygchen
excerpts.content:
Does `MAX_CELLS_IN_EXTENDED_MATRIX` need to be a config value? 
https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/_features/eip7594/das-core.md#data-size

It's based on `MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK` and would need to be increased as well when we increase blob count. May not be an issue (we're not using it atm), but thought worth checking here

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: No not really. That's an artifact of `ExtendedMatrix` which no longer exists. Right now, the config value is used to define the return type for two functions. We could change them to return a `Sequence[MatrixEntry]` instead. Does Lighthouse use an "extended matrix" similar to the spec?

excerpts.author: jimmygchen
excerpts.content: We don't use the intermediate type at the moment, and just transform returned the cells and proofs into `DataColumnSidecars` directly

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: Makes sense. I think most clients do something like that. That configuration value is specific to the spec's implementation, which isn't necessarily the best way to do things.
